- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; cap forecast peak at 1.5–2.0% above prior high.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 3+ consecutive days above 72.0); add 0.3–0.8% buffer to forecast to align with historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days in upward trends; shift forecast up by 0.2–0.5% per lag day if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg -0.1 to 0.1), model tends to overforecast; apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction to avoid overconfidence.
